def.brief: Add one free-function test (test_Q_strict_sites_..., this file's Project harness and helpers, its own __main__ runner) for a case rs-build's verifier found and the suite does not hold: the eyes request when --target is a subdirectory of a larger git repository. Git reports changed names from the repository root while declarations and literal pathspecs are relative to the target; a listing without --relative turned every kept name into a pathspec that matched nothing, so the late-eyes diff was empty. In a repository whose root holds an outer file and a subdirectory project (its own hunsu.lock.json declaring a bare custom-record.json, a hunsu.json replaced by a directory holding a committed child.py, a.py), after a review of the subdirectory and changes to a.py, hunsu.json/child.py, custom-record.json, a reviews/ file and the outer file: the subdirectory's eyes request diff holds a.py's and hunsu.json/child.py's changes, not custom-record.json's, reviews/'s or the outer file's. The build stands (commit 4531a10), so the test passes on the current tree; its red evidence is the same test failing in a copy outside the repository whose dwitbuk.py lacks --relative in the eyes request's name listing (one site, one change — no mutation campaign). Use the real suite or a focused python3 -c run, never python3 -m unittest. Change no repository file but test_dwitbuk.py; do not commit.

non-claims: no check decides this task; done means the agent said so

(provider) The new test covers only the subdirectory case of Q-strict-sites item 4: "The diff is composed from the candidate file paths git reports as changed against the same base (`git diff --name-only`), each judged with `is_record` against `left_out`; only the kept paths are diffed, as literal pathspecs." The section's other sentences are covered by the existing test_Q_strict_sites_* tests, which I did not change.

(provider) The red evidence comes from one hand-made change (removing --relative from the eyes request's name listing), not a mutation campaign. The test does not cover verify_packet, source_state or hooks/stop_eyes.py when the target is a subdirectory.

(provider) `python3 test_dwitbuk.py` exits 1 in this session because AGENT_WORKER=1 is set in the environment, which silences hooks/session_start.py. That makes test_session_start_hook_says_what_the_placed_reviews_still_need_and_nothing_else fail with JSONDecodeError, with or without my change. Run without AGENT_WORKER, the whole suite passes. I did not change that test or the environment.

response.summary:
I added one free-function test to test_dwitbuk.py: `test_Q_strict_sites_eyes_request_in_a_subdirectory_of_a_larger_repository_diffs_by_target_relative_names`. It uses the file's Project, write, git, run, late_packet and STRICT_LOCK helpers, and the file's own __main__ runner picks it up. It runs entirely on real git output.

The setup: a repository whose root holds a committed outer.py and a subdirectory project proj/. proj/ has its own hunsu.lock.json declaring a bare custom-record.json, a hunsu.json that is a directory holding a committed child.py, a.py, and a committed reviews/note.md. After `review --target proj`, the test changes outer.py, proj/a.py, proj/hunsu.json/child.py, proj/custom-record.json and proj/reviews/note.md. It then checks that proj's eyes request diff holds a.py's and hunsu.json/child.py's changes, and none of custom-record.json's, reviews/'s or outer.py's.

Green: it passes on the current tree (commit 4531a10).

Red: I copied dwitbuk.py, eyes_worker.py, hostcall.py, hooks/ and test_dwitbuk.py to a temp directory outside the repository. In the copy I removed only `--relative` from the eyes request's `git diff --name-only` listing (dwitbuk.py:998; diff confirmed one line changed). Running the same test there with python3 -c failed on the a.py assertion with an empty diff ("git names changes from the repository root; the target's own a.py is kept: "). I then deleted the copy.

One fixture detail: the reviews/ file is .md, not .json. dwitbuk.reviews() loads every reviews/*.json as a review, so a committed .json note broke `review` with KeyError 'head' before the eyes request was ever reached.

The check `python3 test_dwitbuk.py` exits 1 in this session because of one failure that was already there: test_session_start_hook_says_what_the_placed_reviews_still_need_and_nothing_else. This session has AGENT_WORKER=1 set, so the session-start hook stays silent and the test's json.loads fails. It fails the same way with my change stashed. With `env -u AGENT_WORKER python3 test_dwitbuk.py`, every test passes, including the new one. I changed only test_dwitbuk.py (+26 lines) and committed nothing.
non-claims: The new test covers only the subdirectory case of Q-strict-sites item 4: "The diff is composed from the candidate file paths git reports as changed against the same base (`git diff --name-only`), each judged with `is_record` against `left_out`; only the kept paths are diffed, as literal pathspecs." The section's other sentences are covered by the existing test_Q_strict_sites_* tests, which I did not change.

The red evidence comes from one hand-made change (removing --relative from the eyes request's name listing), not a mutation campaign. The test does not cover verify_packet, source_state or hooks/stop_eyes.py when the target is a subdirectory.

`python3 test_dwitbuk.py` exits 1 in this session because AGENT_WORKER=1 is set in the environment, which silences hooks/session_start.py. That makes test_session_start_hook_says_what_the_placed_reviews_still_need_and_nothing_else fail with JSONDecodeError, with or without my change. Run without AGENT_WORKER, the whole suite passes. I did not change that test or the environment.
